feature: Dropping a component puts down one instance and nothing else
summary: Dragging a component off the Library now puts down exactly one copy. The original lives in the Library and opens in a space of its own with Edit Original; Done brings you back and every copy follows.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/component-drop-one-instance-walk.json.

try.do: Open the Library on Components and drag the Card tile onto a blank picture.
Drag the Card tile on once more, somewhere else.
Right-click the first Card and choose Edit Original.
With the Card picked, type 40 into Opacity and press Return.
Press Done in the title bar (or Escape twice).
Press Command Z once: both copies come back at full opacity together.
Draw two shapes, group them, press Option Command K, type a name and press Return.

evaluate: After one drag, is it obvious that the single Card on the page is all you got?
Is Done in the middle of the title bar where you look for the way back, the way Figma's main component editing or Sketch's symbol page feels?
When you press Option Command K, is it right that the group stays put as a copy and the new Library tile is the thing picked, ready to name?
Does Make Unique read better than Detach for letting one copy go its own way?
Does the original's space feel like a place of its own, or would you rather see the document dimmed behind it?
rough: Before this, one drag of the Card put two Cards on the page and said the original arrived beside it (2026-10-04-one-instance-drop-before-sc.png).
No mock covers Edit Original's space or its title bar; Done sits in the title bar because that row's one purpose is how you are looking at the window (UX-PATTERNS placement contract, Title bar row).

The copy's button and right-click row now say Make Unique where editor.html and ui-variants.html print Detach, from the user's note on decision a-copy-of-a-component-is-configured-not-authored-when-you-drag-a-component-onto-t (your call on 2026-09-20: "you can right click and make unique").
The space's page is see-through, so it reads as the dark canvas around a lone component rather than as the document's white page.
Escape leaves the space only once nothing is picked, so it takes two presses straight after opening it; Done is one click.
Edit Original and Done Editing Original have menu rows but no shortcut.

Three Components guides (Use it again and again, Override one copy, A button in all its states) still tell you to click the original on the page and stop there; covered by the-components-guides-teach-edit-original-instea.

A file saved with originals on its canvas opens with each one in the Library and a copy standing in exactly the same place, so the page looks identical; an old drop's original beside its copy therefore opens as a second copy you can delete.
